title: Experimental FP8 profile: telemetry-driven selection and automated canary orchestration for Hopper E4M3/E5M2
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a telemetry-driven mechanism to pick between E4M3 and E5M2 FP8 profiles per-model / per-workload, and wire automated canary deployments that detect instability early and trigger safe rollbacks. This ticket experiments with a lightweight scoring scheme, synthetic calibration stress tests, and an automated canary coach that can shadow traffic and flip profiles according to a hysteresis policy. Motivation: current manual selection and ad-hoc canaries are slow; we want a repeatable, observable path to enable FP8 broadly on Hopper while minimizing user-facing regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Implement a per-model telemetry score that combines quality delta (delta-ll), generation entropy, and regression-rate into a single profile_score
Canary pipeline that can run a shadowed FP8 profile on real traffic (5% sampled) and evaluate against golden-seed and reg-suite automatically
Automatic rollback or fallback to INT8 or previous stable FP8 profile when score crosses pre-defined thresholds for more than hysteresis_window
Documentation for operations team and a runbook for manually intervening in canary failures
End-to-end test that injects quantization noise and validates the canary detects degradation and executes fallback
notes: Design trade-offs: a lightweight score is preferred for runtime evaluation (cheap to compute in observability pipeline) over expensive full-reference comparisons. We weight delta-ll higher for conversational workloads and regression-rate higher for completion workloads.
We will avoid changing kernel selection logic in this ticket; focus is profile selection and orchestration. Kernel tuning is tracked separately.
Calibration work: we run a fast local re-calibration (10k samples) during canary to detect gross mismatches; full calibration pipeline remains offline.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Define score and telemetry events (delta-ll, avg-token-entropy, regression-rate, latency-delta). Instrument model endpoints to emit these metrics.
Phase 2: Canary runner: shadow 5% traffic to FP8 profile variant (E4M3 or E5M2) and compute score every 15m window. Run fast local calibration and synthetic noise tests concurrently.
Phase 3: Orchestration: build automated rules - if score < -0.02 for two consecutive windows (15m each) then trigger rollback. Add 15m hysteresis before re-attempt.
Phase 4: Validation: run golden-seed (2k prompts), reg-suite (10k), and randomized stress cases; evaluate detection precision and false-positive rate < 2%.
Phase 5: Docs & Runbook: publish operational checklist, add Slack alerts and escalation playbook.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives causing unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: Use two-window confirmation and require fail on both golden-seed and reg-suite before automatic rollback for high-risk models.
Risk: Telemetry noise on bursty workloads. Mitigation: Normalize by context-length and use robust median aggregation instead of mean for short windows.
Risk: Calibration runtime overhead. Mitigation: Fast local calibration limited to 10k samples; heavy calibration runs remain offline and are scheduled off-peak.
Risk: Edge-case models that prefer E5M2 but show initial delta-ll because of input distribution shift. Mitigation: Allow per-model whitelist/exemptions and manual approval flow in console.
